mainEntity.name: Why does a² + b² = c² only work for right triangles?

acceptedAnswer.text: The general rule is the Law of Cosines, c² = a² + b² − 2ab·cos C. For a right angle, cos 90° = 0 and the last term disappears. For an acute angle c² is smaller than a² + b²; for an obtuse angle it is larger.

mainEntity.name: What is a primitive Pythagorean triple?

acceptedAnswer.text: A set of whole numbers (a, b, c) with a² + b² = c² whose greatest common divisor is 1, such as 3-4-5 or 5-12-13. Multiples like 6-8-10 are still triples but not primitive.

mainEntity.name: How do I find the distance between two points in 3D?

acceptedAnswer.text: Square the differences in x, y and z, add them, and take the square root. It is the Pythagorean theorem applied twice, and it also gives the space diagonal of a box with edges Δx, Δy and Δz.

mainEntity.name: What does an exact radical answer like 6√2 mean?

acceptedAnswer.text: When the number under the root is not a perfect square, the root is irrational. It can be simplified by pulling out square factors: √72 = √(36 × 2) = 6√2, which equals about 8.4853. The exact form avoids rounding.

mainEntity.name: Can the hypotenuse be shorter than a leg?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. The hypotenuse is always the longest side of a right triangle, because c² = a² + b² is larger than either a² or b². When solving for a leg, the hypotenuse you enter must exceed the known leg.

mainEntity.name: Does it work for any units?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, as long as all sides use the same unit. The result is in that unit; areas are in square units. The unit-equivalent panel converts the answer to other common lengths.
